content:
The Quadratic Equations chapter is a high-yield part of the CAT Quantitative Aptitude section, and a favourite in XAT, SNAP, NMAT and CMAT too. This guide explains what CAT Quadratic Equations tests, the formulas and shortcuts worth memorising, the mistakes that cost marks, and a free 10-question online test you can take right now.

Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CAT asks on Quadratic Equations

Roots and their nature (discriminant), Vieta’s sum/product relations, forming equations from roots and maxima/minima of quadratics.

Key formulas & shortcuts

  • Roots: x = (−b ± √(b²−4ac))/(2a); D = b²−4ac.
  • D>0 real distinct, D=0 real equal, D<0 complex.
  • Sum of roots = −b/a, product = c/a.
  • Equation with roots α, β: x² − (α+β)x + αβ = 0.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Sign errors in −b/a for the sum of roots.
  • Forgetting D=0 is the equal-roots (tangency) case.
  • Dropping the ± in the quadratic formula.

quiz.title: CAT Quadratic Equations Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten CAT-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: If a,b,c are odd integers and ax²+bx+c=0 has real roots, then
questions.explanation: b²-4ac: an odd square is ≡1 (mod 8) and 4ac≡4 (mod 8), so the discriminant ≡5 (mod 8), which is never a perfect square. Hence the (real) roots are irrational.

questions.q: If x²+ax+bc=0 and x²+bx+ca=0 ( a≠ b ) have a common root, then their other roots satisfy
questions.explanation: Subtracting gives (a-b)x+c(b-a)=0⇒ x=c (common root). Then the other roots are b and a (from the products bc and ca ). The equation with roots a,b is x²-(a+b)x+ab; since a+b=-c, it is x²+cx+ab=0.

questions.q: f(x)=((x-b)(x-c))/((x-a)) ( a,b,c distinct reals) assumes all real values provided
options: c lies between a and b
a lies between b and c
b lies between a and c
questions.explanation: Setting f(x)=y gives a quadratic in x; it has real x for every real y iff its discriminant is always ≥0, which holds iff a lies between b and c.

questions.q: If a∈ℝ⁻ and a≠-2, then the equation x²+a|x|+1=0
options: must have exactly two real roots
must have either exactly two real roots or no real roots
must have either four real roots or no real roots
questions.explanation: Put t=|x|≥0: t²+at+1=0 has product 1 0 and sum -a>0. If a<-2 (discriminant >0 ) both roots are positive, giving 4 real x; if -2<a<0 no real t, so no real roots.

questions.q: The equations ax²-2bx+c=0, bx²-2cx+a=0 and cx²-2ax+b=0 will have only positive roots, provided
questions.explanation: Adding the three equations and analysing the discriminant conditions (each must be ≥0 ) forces a=b=c; only then do all three have (equal, positive) real roots.

questions.q: If the sum of the roots of ax²+bx+c=0 equals the sum of the squares of their reciprocals, then (b²)/(ac)+(bc)/(a²) is
questions.explanation: The condition α+β=(1)/(α²)+(1)/(β²) simplifies (with α+β=-b/a, αβ=c/a ) to ab²+bc²=2a²c. Dividing by a²c gives (b²)/(ac)+(bc)/(a²)=2.

questions.q: The total number of values of x satisfying (√3+1)²ˣ+(√3-1)²ˣ=2³ˣ is
questions.explanation: Rewrite as (4+2√3)ˣ+(4-2√3)ˣ=8ˣ. Dividing by 4ˣ gives a strictly monotonic balance satisfied only at x=1 (check: 8=8 ). So exactly one value.

questions.q: If α,β,γ are the roots of x³-x²-1=0, then (1+α)/(1-α)+(1+β)/(1-β)+(1+γ)/(1-γ) equals
If α,β are the roots of x²+px+q=0 and α⁴,β⁴ are the roots of x²-rx+s=0, then the equation x²-4qx+(2q²-r)=0 has always
options: one positive and one negative root
questions.explanation: Its discriminant is 16q²-4(2q²-r)=4(2q²+r). Since r=α⁴+β⁴=(p²-2q)²-2q², we get 2q²+r=(p²-2q)²≥0, so the discriminant is ≥0 — the equation always has two real roots.

questions.q: If α,β are roots of x²+px+q=0 and α⁴,β⁴ are roots of x²-rx+s=0, then x²-4qx+2q²-r=0 always has
options: one positive and one negative root
questions.explanation: With r=α⁴+β⁴=(p²-2q)²-2q², the discriminant is 4(p²-2q)²≥0, so there are always two real roots.

faq.q: What does the discriminant tell you?
faq.a: D>0 gives two real distinct roots, D=0 two equal roots, D<0 a complex conjugate pair.

faq.q: How to form a quadratic from its roots?
faq.a: Use x² − (sum)x + (product) = 0 with sum = α+β and product = αβ.
